findings.finding: RND.POST.effects puts the post chain (bloom, depth of field, motion blur, lens) 'after tonemapping on display-referred output'. That is the LDR-era order. It also contradicts C-TRANSLUCENT, which composes translucency 'before/after DOF and upscale', and the upscalers in C-TEMPORAL, which take pre-tonemap HDR input. An agent writing the SKILL.md from this row would build a display-referred post chain: highlights clip, bloom stops following exposure, and the chain breaks when one scene feeds several HDR/SDR output transforms.
findings.evidence: Jimenez, 'Next-Gen Post-Processing in CoD:AW' (SIGGRAPH 2014 Advances). The UE and Frostbite post pipelines run bloom, DOF and motion blur before the tonemapper. In ACES/OCIO the output transform is the last scene-to-display step. DLSS, FSR and XeSS integration guides require pre-tonemap HDR input.
findings.proposed_change: Rename RND.POST.effects to 'Post chain on scene-referred linear HDR before the output transform; ordering vs upscaling published in C-SCENETEX phases'. Add RND.POST.display-referred (grain, dithering and UI-safe sharpening after the output transform). Add the scene-referred/display-referred boundary to the C-COLOR summary.

findings.finding: The only shadow-map capability is RND.LIGHT.vsm, which is std3d-only. rt-shadows is also std3d, and contact shadows are screen-space only. No row exists for cascaded shadow maps, local-light shadow atlases or shadow caching. Every lite3d configuration therefore closes with no directional or local shadow-map technique. Cascades appear only in the skill's purpose text and in gap-analysis B4, and that ADR can only choose among owned capabilities.
findings.evidence: CSM/PSSM (Engel; Zhang), scrolling or cached cascades and shadow atlases are what ships on mobile, Switch-class hardware, standalone XR and non-VSM PC tiers. The Arm and Qualcomm TBDR guides describe them. UE keeps CSM as the mobile and non-Nanite path next to VSM.
findings.proposed_change: Add three capabilities owned by direct-lighting-shadows, each E with no profile: RND.LIGHT.csm (cascaded/scrolling directional shadows with stabilization and caching), RND.LIGHT.local-shadows (atlas and cube maps, static/dynamic caching, per-light budget) and RND.LIGHT.shadow-filtering (PCF/PCSS/EVSM tiers). Add to the C-LIGHT summary: 'shadow technique per tier behind one lookup API'.

findings.target: vfx-particles, C-ABILITY, C-SEQ, C-ANIM, destruction-fracture, atmosphere-weather, ui-architect
findings.finding: vfx-particles provides no contract. Nothing lets gameplay cues, animation notifies, destruction, sequencer tracks, weather or UI spawn, attach, parameterize, pool or stop effects. Nothing declares how VFX reads its data sources either: skinned surfaces, physics contacts, environment fields. Audio has C-AUDIO for the same job, and VFX has no counterpart. Consumers will reach into VFX internals or each invent a spawn API, and there is no place for cosmetic-vs-simulated or significance rules on effect requests.
findings.evidence: Niagara exposes a component/parameter API and Data Interfaces, and GAS routes GameplayCues to Niagara. Unity VFX Graph exposes event attributes and property binders. Frostbite and Decima VFX talks describe effect-request interfaces with budgets.
findings.proposed_change: Add C-VFX (layer 3, owner vfx-particles, requires C-RSCENE, conformance, oracle_author gameplay-systems-toolkit): batched effect-instance requests with pooled handles, user parameters, event payloads, data-source bindings (deformation streams, C-PHYS contacts, C-ENV fields), significance and budget class, determinism class. Add C-VFX? to the consumes of gameplay-systems-toolkit, cinematics-sequencer, destruction-fracture, animation-runtime, atmosphere-weather and ui-architect. Add C-ANIM? and C-PHYS? to vfx-particles.

findings.target: C-VT, texture-streaming-vt, material-system, geometry-pipeline, translucency-decals, vfx-particles, RND.TEX.mip-streaming
findings.finding: C-VT is consumed only by terrain and render-2d-vector. material-system generates the shader code that samples VT page tables and writes sampler/VT feedback, and it does not consume C-VT. Neither do geometry-pipeline (visibility-buffer resolve), decals or VFX. texture-streaming-vt consumes no scene or view contract (no C-RSCENE, C-INSTANCES or C-VIEW). CPU-computed mip priorities are the established path on lite3d, where sampler feedback is std3d-only, and they therefore have no data path. Either materials cannot sample streamed or virtual textures, or the streamer cannot know what to stream.
findings.evidence: UE texture streaming computes per-primitive texel factors from the render scene and views. UE SVT/RVT and id's virtual texturing inject VT sampling and feedback into generated material code. D3D12 sampler feedback needs shader-side writes emitted by the material compiler.
findings.proposed_change: Add C-VT to material-system consumes. Add C-VT? to geometry-pipeline, translucency-decals and vfx-particles. Add C-RSCENE, C-INSTANCES? and C-VIEW to texture-streaming-vt consumes. Extend the C-VT summary with 'shader-side VT sampling/feedback interface for material codegen; per-instance texel-density registration for CPU-priority mip streaming'.

findings.finding: RND.GRAPH.external-work declares acceleration-structure builds as producers that the render graph schedules, with barriers, queue placement and budgets. But C-RTAS (build/refit/compaction and ray queries) is layer 2, below C-RG (layer 3), and the C-RTAS module does not consume C-RG (only C-RG@C-RT does). The layering therefore forbids the AS-build module from registering with the graph, so it must record its own barriers and submissions. That reintroduces renderer sync outside the graph (L28), including for the non-render consumer spatial-audio-acoustics.
findings.evidence: AS builds need AS/UAV barriers against the passes that trace, and they compete for async compute and scratch memory. UE RDG and Frostbite FrameGraph schedule BLAS/TLAS builds as graph passes. C-MLGPU already follows the correct pattern: layer 3, requires C-RG.
findings.proposed_change: Move C-RTAS to layer 3 with requires [C-RG, C-GPUMEM], and make ray-tracing-infrastructure consume C-RG unattributed. Alternatively, add an L2 contract C-GPUWORK owned by render-graph-scheduling (external GPU work registration: producer, queue class, deadline, budget, resource import/export). C-RTAS, C-GPUMEM uploads and C-IO GPU decompression would require it, and the graph would implement it.

findings.target: path-tracing, RND.PT.reference, QA.RENDER.reference, ANM.CINE.movie-render, render-validation, cinematics-sequencer
findings.finding: The reference path tracer is the ground-truth oracle for all raster features, yet it provides no contract. render-validation and cinematics movie render reach it through no declared interface (convergence target, seeds, AOVs, tolerance). The oracle also consumes C-LIGHT (the sampling API of direct-lighting-shadows, one of the skills it judges) and C-TEMPORAL (the denoiser/upscaler). A light-units or IES bug in C-LIGHT, or a denoiser bias, therefore appears identically in raster and reference, and the goldens pass. The oracle is not independent of what it grades. It also shares a lead and a workstream with the judged features.
findings.evidence: PBRT-4 and Mitsuba references, and UE's reference path tracer, evaluate lights and BSDFs from scene definitions, not from real-time light grids, and do not denoise references. The framework's own oracle-independence rule is L56 / QA.AGENT.oracle-independence.
findings.proposed_change: Add C-PTREF (layer 3, owner path-tracing, requires C-RSCENE and C-MATIF, conformance, oracle_author render-validation): reference render request (scene snapshot, view, convergence criterion, seed, AOVs) and converged, undenoised output with a variance estimate. Attribute C-LIGHT and C-TEMPORAL to the real-time module only. render-validation and cinematics-sequencer consume C-PTREF?. Add an independence row: path-tracing vs direct-lighting-shadows/global-illumination, no shared sampling code.

findings.target: RND.GEO.splat-relight, RND.GEO.splats, radar 'Gaussian splatting & radiance fields'
findings.finding: Relightable and dynamic splats with hybrid raster/RT composition are labelled E and enabled in all std3d shipping configurations. Static splats in the same skill are only M. The radar's promotion trigger for splats requires relighting and shipped use, and docs/07 calls splatting experimental for games. Because the row is E, it bypasses the radar and fallback check and becomes a silent dependency of shipping builds.
findings.evidence: Relightable 3D Gaussians, GS³ (2024), 3DGRT/3DGUT (2024–25) and dynamic/4D GS are still research. No shipped game relies on relit, dynamic splats.
findings.proposed_change: Set RND.GEO.splat-relight to maturity X with profile ['experimental']. Add it to a radar entry with fallback 'static unlit splats composited over raster, or photogrammetry meshes'.

findings.finding: One M row merges established spatiotemporal denoisers with emerging ML ray reconstruction. The radar fallback, 'Spatiotemporal denoisers', is part of the same M capability, so the fallback is circular, and the established path every RT tier needs sits behind an emerging label.
findings.evidence: NRD ReBLUR/ReLAX and SVGF (Schied 2017) are widely shipped. DLSS RR is vendor-specific.
findings.proposed_change: Split into RND.RECON.denoise (spatiotemporal, E) and RND.RECON.ml-denoise (ML / joint ray reconstruction, M). Point the radar entry at ml-denoise, with fallback RND.RECON.denoise.

findings.target: radar entries for RND.SHADER.neural and RND.SHADER.autodiff
findings.finding: RND.SHADER.autodiff shares a radar entry whose fallback, 'Standalone inference dispatch', does not apply to compile-time differentiation. The evidence, 'SM 6.9 cooperative vectors (preview)', is stale: cooperative vectors did not ship in retail SM 6.9 and were redirected to a broader DXIL linear-algebra feature, and Vulkan's cooperative-vector extension is NV-only. A trigger keyed to 'cooperative vectors' may never fire.
findings.evidence: DirectX Developer Blog: SM 6.9 release and linear-algebra roadmap (2025). Khronos registry: VK_NV_cooperative_vector and VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix.
findings.proposed_change: Give autodiff its own M radar entry (fallback: hand-derived gradients / finite differences in tool code). Reword the neural entry's evidence and trigger to 'API-neutral matrix/tensor intrinsics (DXIL linear algebra, VK cooperative matrix/vector, Metal tensor ops) on ≥2 vendors'.

findings.finding: The catalogue has no pattern for the display-referred/LDR pipeline, which has already leaked into RND.POST.effects (see K-RENDER-1). It also has no pattern for geometry-shader, HW-tessellation or stream-out pipelines on capable tiers. L29 omits the capabilities that actually carry the PSO stance: RND.SHADER.precache and RND.RHI.pso.
findings.evidence: AMD RDNA and NVIDIA performance guides discourage geometry shaders and HW tessellation in favour of mesh/compute. HDR output requires a scene-referred pipeline. UE 5.2+ PSO precaching is the load-time half of the PSO stance.
findings.proposed_change: Add L58 'Display-referred/LDR pipeline' (owner post-color-hdr; stance_capabilities RND.POST.color, RND.POST.effects). Add L59 'GS/HW-tessellation/stream-out on capable tiers' (owner geometry-pipeline; stance_capabilities RND.GEO.mesh-shaders, RND.LOD.displacement). Add RND.SHADER.precache and RND.RHI.pso to L29.

findings.finding: No capability covers load-time transcoding from supercompressed universal formats to device formats. WebGPU exposes BC, ASTC or ETC2 depending on browser and device, and Android is similarly fragmented. Transcoding appears only as an NTC fallback phrase.
findings.evidence: Khronos KTX 2.0 and glTF KHR_texture_basisu. Basis Universal is used by three.js, Babylon and Unity web builds.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.TEX.transcode 'Load-time transcoding from KTX2/UASTC/ETC1S per device capability' (E), owned by texture-streaming-vt with contributors platform-web and asset-cook-processors. Cover the transcoder under the existing assets/user-images untrusted-input entries.

findings.finding: K-RENDER's scope leaves out world-editor-viewport and visual-debugging-tools, which own the rendering-tooling surface (debug draw, GPU overlays, capture integration). It also leaves out text-fonts, which owns the glyph atlas/curve data behind C-DRAW2D. None of these gets a rendering review.
findings.evidence: RND.ARCH.editor-rendering, RND.TOOL.frame-debugger and RND.SHADER.gpu-debug-draw all list these skills as contributors.
findings.proposed_change: Add world-editor-viewport, visual-debugging-tools and text-fonts to K-RENDER scope, with stages S1–S3.

findings.target: contracts.json oracle_author (40/110, e.g. C-TYPES, C-MOD, C-MEM, C-SYNC, C-ID, C-RHI, C-SHADER, C-MATIF, C-RT, C-NETLINK, C-REP, C-PREDICT, C-SERVER, C-SHARD, C-NAV, C-SCRIPT, C-SAVE, C-GAMEDATA, C-ABILITY, C-AI, C-CROWD, C-AUTOMATION, C-PKG, C-TESTHOST); crosscutting.json independence; ARCH.ORG.independence; ARCH.ORG.staffing; docs/00 §2
findings.finding: docs/00 §2 says implementer-vs-oracle independence is enforced by keeping each pair in different workstreams, because the workstream is the co-hosting unit. The data does not do this. In 40 contracts the oracle author shares the owner's or implementers' workstream, and in some it is the implementer's own lead (C-TYPES→core-runtime-architect, C-TESTHOST→test-architect, C-PKG→build-release-architect, C-AUTOMATION→editor-architect, C-CROWD→gameplay-architect). For C-RHI, all 5 backends and the oracle author gpu-memory-resources are in 'rendering'. The matrix only contains the sentinel pair (test-architect, owning-skill), and check.py only rejects oracle == sole implementer. Under ARCH.ORG.staffing co-hosting, one agent writes both the implementation and its acceptance suite.
findings.evidence: This contradicts the framework's own anti-gaming stance (§6 last row, QA.AGENT.oracle-independence). Implementers grading tests they control is the named failure mode, and small co-hosted setups create it by construction.
findings.proposed_change: Generate per-contract independence pairs (oracle_author vs owner and vs each implementer) and require different workstreams in check.py. Reassign the 40 same-workstream oracle authors, preferably to quality-workstream validators. Fix the §2 wording until the data matches it.

findings.target: oracle_author of C-PAL(accessibility), C-EDHOST(fluid-simulation), C-SIGN(modding-ugc), C-ML(anti-cheat-integrity), C-RTAS(spatial-audio-acoustics), C-VEHICLE(audio-content-runtime), C-ECS(audio-architect), C-RES(audio-dsp-mixing), C-DET(character-movement), C-FRAME(ai-behavior-perception), C-MATH(animation-runtime), C-INTEGRITY(platform-services), C-GPUMEM(async-io-storage)
findings.finding: These oracle authors look chosen to pass the 'not sole implementer' check, not for competence. Peripheral consumers with no domain expertise write the acceptance suites for foundational contracts. Examples: PAL suspend/clock/QoS conformance is written by accessibility; crypto and signature conformance by modding; determinism float and ordered-reduction rules by a movement skill; the frame scheduler by AI; the editor host by a fluid solver.
findings.evidence: Consumer-driven contract testing (Pact-style) adds consumer cases; it does not make one consumer the acceptance authority. C-TEST already merges consumer-contributed cases. Crypto conformance needs KAT/Wycheproof-class vectors. A single consumer omits everything its slice does not use.
findings.proposed_change: Choose oracle authors by competence plus independence: render contracts→render-validation; physics/anim/audio/net/C-DET/C-SNAPSHOT/C-REPLAY→simulation-validation; C-SIGN→security-engineering; L0–L2 foundation (C-PAL, C-MEM, C-TASK, C-FRAME, C-ECS, C-RES, C-IO, C-GPUMEM)→new quality expert 'foundation-conformance' (or robustness-fuzzing); editor contracts→functional-automation-soak. Add a per-contract consumer_cases list.

findings.target: ARCH.ORG.escalation; docs/00 §2; skills.json workstreams rendering, simulation, content, quality, online, foundation
findings.finding: Six workstreams contain more than one lead or cross-cutting subtree: render+gpu-platform, physics+animation, content-pipeline+resource-streaming, test+security, network+security (anti-cheat), core+4 cross-cutting. A cross-lead dispute inside one workstream is neither inside one subtree nor cross-workstream, so no arbiter is named. These are the highest-friction seams: ragdoll/root motion; ray-tracing-infrastructure under gpu-platform binding render-architect's C-RSCENE/C-INSTANCES; cook vs runtime format; anti-cheat validators vs replication.
findings.evidence: With ~150 agents, an unrouted dispute class either stalls or falls back to engine-architect, which defeats delegated arbitration.
findings.proposed_change: Add an 'arbiter' per workstream in skills.json (e.g. rendering→render-architect, simulation→physics-architect with animation-architect as co-signer on sim-schedule, content→resource-streaming-architect for runtime and content-pipeline-architect for cook), or state explicitly in ARCH.ORG.escalation that same-workstream cross-lead disputes go to engine-architect. Have check.py require an arbiter for every multi-lead workstream.

findings.target: ui-architect (21 caps UI.FW.*), content-pipeline-architect (20 caps incl. CNT.COOK.ddc/distributed/shared-cache/world-build/on-demand), physics-architect (18 caps incl. PHY.ARCH.rewind/streaming/async/events/fields/multi-world/local-frames/tier-transitions), platform-architect (27)
findings.finding: Several leads are also the main implementers of large subsystems, and they arbitrate disputes in their own subtree while being a party to them. ui-architect owns the whole retained UI runtime (layout, styling, animation, world UI, maps, loading screens, subtitle presentation) and there is no UI runtime expert. content-pipeline-architect owns DDC, distributed cook and the cook server. physics-architect owns rewind, streaming insertion, fields, multi-world and local frames.
findings.evidence: This goes against the brief's 'few orchestrators, many focused experts' and the framework's own decider-vs-party separation. Production UI runtimes (Gameface, Noesis, Slate, UI Toolkit) and DDC/cook-server infrastructure (Zen server, Bazel-class caches) are separate specialties.
findings.proposed_change: Add expert 'ui-runtime-framework' owning UI.FW.layout/styling/animation/world-ui/performance/maps/loading-screens/subtitles/validation. Add tool expert 'cook-infrastructure' owning CNT.COOK.ddc/distributed/shared-cache/on-demand/world-build. Add expert 'physics-world-runtime' owning PHY.ARCH.rewind/streaming/async/events/fields/multi-world/local-frames/tier-transitions. Leads keep policy and contract ownership.

findings.target: gameplay-systems-toolkit purpose; gameplay-camera; GAM.CAM.rigs; GAM.CAM.photo; C-VIEW (oracle_author, consumes)
findings.finding: gameplay-systems-toolkit's purpose still claims 'camera system … photo mode', which gameplay-camera owns (GAM.CAM.rigs, GAM.CAM.photo). Its non-responsibilities route only cinematic cameras away. It consumes C-VIEW as mandatory and is C-VIEW's oracle author, a leftover of the old ownership. Two generated SKILL.md files would both claim camera rigs and photo mode.
findings.evidence: The SKILL.md is generated from the purpose, so a wording overlap becomes double ownership that check.py (capability rows only) cannot see.
findings.proposed_change: Remove 'camera system' and 'photo mode' from the gameplay-systems-toolkit purpose. Add the non-responsibility ['Gameplay cameras & photo mode','gameplay-camera']. Make its C-VIEW dependency optional ('C-VIEW?'). Reassign C-VIEW's oracle_author to a non-consumer validator.

findings.target: C-PHYS summary; C-MOVE; GAM.MOVE.modes; GAM.MOVE.root-motion; character-physics; character-movement
findings.finding: The C-PHYS summary (L3) includes 'character controllers (movement modes, move requests, root-motion hand-off)'. Those belong to C-MOVE (L4, character-movement), and character-physics' own non-responsibility routes movement modes to character-movement. The physics contract therefore leaks a gameplay-layer concept, and two contracts define the move request and the root-motion hand-off.
findings.evidence: This follows the established split: a physics collide-and-slide primitive (Jolt CharacterVirtual, PhysX CCT) underneath a gameplay movement component with modes (Unreal CharacterMovementComponent).
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite C-PHYS as 'character controller primitive: desired displacement → resolved displacement, ground/step/slope sensing, platform interaction'. Keep movement modes, move requests and root-motion hand-off in C-MOVE only.

findings.target: CORE.OBJ.events; C-ID summary; entity-object-model purpose; legacy L19; C-FLOW; CORE.OBJ.world-instances; GAM.SYS.messages
findings.finding: CORE.OBJ.events says 'global event bus with immediate synchronous listener dispatch by default'. This contradicts L19, which names this row as its stance capability with the stance 'deferred batched events at declared consumption points'. It also contradicts C-FLOW as the default data path, the no-hidden-globals and multi-world stances, and ARCH.STRUCT.binding. GAM.SYS.messages builds on it.
findings.evidence: Immediate cross-subsystem callbacks run mid-update on the producer's thread, which serializes the task graph and hides races. Modern engines drain deferred queues at schedule points (Bevy events/observers, DOTS ECB, Mass signals).
findings.proposed_change: CORE.OBJ.events → 'world-scoped typed batched event channels drained at declared C-FRAME consumption points; synchronous dispatch only intra-subsystem by ADR'. Align the C-ID summary.

findings.target: PHY.ARCH.stepping; physics-architect purpose; CORE.FRAME.fixed-step; legacy L30; C-PHYS conformance
findings.finding: PHY.ARCH.stepping says 'Variable-timestep stepping on the render frame delta'. L30 lists that as legacy. The C-PHYS conformance clause (resimulate N ticks reproduces the state hash), PHY.ARCH.rewind, rollback and lockstep all need a fixed or declared step.
findings.evidence: Fiedler, 'Fix Your Timestep'; Jolt, Havok and PhysX guidance; every shipped rollback title.
findings.proposed_change: PHY.ARCH.stepping → 'Fixed/declared-step physics on the C-FRAME simulation clock with substepping and interpolation to render time'. Add it to L30's stance_capabilities.

findings.target: CNT.COOK.ddc; content-pipeline-architect purpose; CNT.COOK.incremental-equivalence; CNT.COOK.shared-cache; untrusted-inputs shared-ddc; C-COOK
findings.finding: The DDC is 'keyed by source path & file modification time'. This contradicts the owner's purpose ('content-addressed store'), the shared-ddc registry entry ('content-addressed/verified') and incremental equals clean cook. Path/mtime keys return stale or wrong artifacts across machines, after checkouts, under clock skew and after processor version changes.
findings.evidence: Unreal DDC keys (processor version plus input hashes), Bazel/Buck2 action keys and Zen storage are all content-addressed.
findings.proposed_change: CNT.COOK.ddc → 'keyed by content hash of all inputs + processor version + parameters + target platform; path/mtime only as a local stat-cache accelerator'.

findings.target: CORE.JOBS.blocking; C-TASK blocking rules; RES.MGMT.no-stall; CORE.JOBS.pinned; CORE.JOBS.priorities
findings.finding: CORE.JOBS.blocking says 'Blocking & long-running tasks run inline on work-stealing workers (no dedicated lanes or compensating threads)'. A blocking call on a worker takes that core out of the frame graph; N blocked tasks starve or deadlock the frame. This contradicts the latency lanes, pinned lanes and the no-stall stance.
findings.evidence: TBB arenas/isolation, .NET thread-pool injection, Unreal background/named-thread priorities, and fiber waits that yield (Naughty Dog, GDC 2015).
findings.proposed_change: CORE.JOBS.blocking → 'frame tasks never block; waits yield (fiber/coroutine) or run on a bounded long-running/blocking lane budgeted in the thread inventory'.

findings.finding: PLAT.WEB.runtime requires SharedArrayBuffer and 'assumes cross-origin isolation on every host'. CORE.JOBS.degenerate exists to run the task graph on 0–2 workers for the web, so the single-threaded web path has no platform-side owner.
findings.evidence: Many web game portals, iframes and CDNs cannot set COOP/COEP. Godot 4.3+ and Unity ship no-threads web exports for this reason.
findings.proposed_change: PLAT.WEB.runtime → 'WASM threads when cross-origin isolated; single-threaded inline build variant otherwise; host capability detection'. Add a no-COI web configuration to the checked set.

findings.target: UI.LOC.strings; C-LOC; crosscutting localizability obligation; GAM.NARR.lines
findings.finding: UI.LOC.strings keys string tables by English source text. That contradicts C-LOC 'String IDs', the owner's own 'stable string IDs' obligation and the narrative line IDs. Fixing an English typo invalidates every translation, and homographs collide.
findings.evidence: Unreal FText namespace+key, Unity Localization key tables, XLIFF resname.
findings.proposed_change: UI.LOC.strings → 'String tables keyed by stable IDs (namespace+key) with source text, context and max-length metadata'.

findings.finding: Budgets are 'measured on the reference high-end PC and scaled proportionally to lower tiers'. C-BUDGET and the owner's purpose define budgets per tier × configuration × refresh class. Proportional scaling fails for TBDR, UMA, thermal limits and CPU-submitted tiers, which run different code paths.
findings.evidence: Mobile budgets are set on target devices at sustained thermal state (Arm and Qualcomm guidance); console budgets are measured on the console.
findings.proposed_change: PRF.METH.budgets → 'per-tier budgets derived from the performance model and validated on each tier's reference device at sustained state; never scaled from another tier'.

findings.finding: 'Automatic retry until green; the owning skill quarantines persistent offenders' turns races and nondeterminism into passes. It also lets the implementer quarantine its own tests, which undermines test-integrity and oracle independence.
findings.evidence: Google flaky-test research; Chromium and Mozilla practice of bounded retries, recorded flakes and quarantine decided by the test owner.
findings.proposed_change: QA.STRAT.flaky → 'bounded retry recording the flake as a failure signal; quarantine decided by oracle_author/test-architect with expiry; flake rate is a gate metric'.

findings.finding: C-GAMEDATA (gameplay-data) claims 'gameplay tag registry and tag queries', but the tags capability belongs to gameplay-systems-toolkit and C-ABILITY also exposes tag queries. Two contracts define one tag namespace.
findings.evidence: A tag registry must be a single namespace (Unreal GameplayTagsManager).
findings.proposed_change: Remove the tag registry from C-GAMEDATA, or move GAM.SYS.tags and the tag-dictionary tooling to gameplay-data and drop tags from C-ABILITY. Choose one.

findings.target: global-illumination purpose vs RND.RT.sdf-scene; fluid-simulation purpose vs WLD.ENV.water-interaction; PRF.BENCH.regression/perf-benchmarking purpose vs BLD.CI.bisection; C-TYPES summary vs CORE.TYPES.crypto/C-SIGN; C-NETLINK 'sessions' vs C-NETSESSION; C-AI vs C-ENV 'environment query service'
findings.finding: Residual wording overlaps: GI claims 'SDF scene representations' (owned by ray-tracing-infrastructure); fluid-simulation claims 'shallow-water simulation' (owned by water-ocean); perf-benchmarking claims bisection (ARCH.ORG.triage names BLD.CI.bisection the single engine); C-TYPES still mentions a crypto wrapper (garbled 'hashinggraphic'); C-NETLINK is titled 'links & sessions'; C-AI and C-ENV both call themselves an 'environment query service'.
findings.evidence: Purposes and summaries become SKILL.md and contract text, so each is a second claim on territory owned elsewhere.
findings.proposed_change: GI: 'consumes SDF/software ray queries via C-RTAS'. fluid-simulation: drop 'shallow-water'. PRF.BENCH.regression: 'detection; bisection via BLD.CI.bisection'. C-TYPES: drop crypto. C-NETLINK: rename to 'links & channels'. C-AI: 'AI tactical/environment queries (EQS class)'.

findings.target: non_responsibilities of robustness-fuzzing, ml-inference-runtime, gpu-platform-architect, research-evidence, certification-compliance, gpu-performance, render-validation
findings.finding: These non-responsibilities route to a real skill but the wrong one: 'Fixing parsers→serialization-schema' (the registry has 40+ validating owners); 'GPU queue/budget arbitration of C-MLGPU→gpu-platform-architect' (it owns no such capability; RND.GRAPH.async/external-work belong to render-graph-scheduling); gpu-platform-architect's backend list omits rhi-console; research-evidence routes 'decision (the owning skill does)' to architecture-governance; certification-compliance routes 'platform features' to platform-architect; gpu-performance and render-validation route feature fixes to render-architect instead of owning-skill.
findings.evidence: Misroutes push work to leads without the territory, which creates escalation noise across ~150 agents.
findings.proposed_change: Retarget to owning-skill, render-graph-scheduling and the platform experts, and add rhi-console to the list. Extend check.py so a specific-skill route must name a skill that owns or leads a capability in the routed area.

findings.finding: Refresh-rate selection and pacing is claimed by three owners: platform-mobile ('frame pacing & refresh-rate selection'), the runtime-scalability actuator ('frame-rate cap/refresh selection') and frame-orchestration pacing. The thermal row was already reduced to a signal backend; frame pacing was not.
findings.evidence: Swappy and preferredFrameRateRange are PAL mechanisms. Selection belongs to one governor loop and the timeline to C-PRESENT.
findings.proposed_change: PLAT.MOB.frame-pacing → 'mobile present-rate/pacing backends implementing C-PRESENT/C-PAL; no independent selection'.

findings.finding: PHY.FLUID.cellular is 'grid/cellular … 2D-capable', but its skill is only included with aaa, sandbox or massim. A min2d falling-sand game must add 'sandbox', which pulls in the 3D voxel-worlds skill with mandatory C-WORLD, C-PHYS and C-PCG.
findings.evidence: The brief requires scale-down, and cellular simulation is the defining mechanic of several 2D indie titles.
findings.proposed_change: Add min2d to fluid-simulation and tag PHY.FLUID.particles/grid/gpu with aaa/sandbox at capability level, or move PHY.FLUID.cellular into systems-simulation next to GAM.SIM.fields. Add a min2d configuration that exercises it.

findings.finding: The id says staged-rollout but the text says 'Simultaneous global rollout to all players with post-release kill switches'. Kill switches only act after every player has already received the release.
findings.evidence: Standard practice: Play staged rollouts, App Store phased release, canary server fleets.
findings.proposed_change: BLD.REL.staged-rollout → 'staged/percentage rollouts (store phased release, canary fleets) with health gates, halt/rollback and kill switches'.

findings.finding: CORE.JOBS.blocking says blocking and long-running tasks 'run inline on work-stealing workers (no dedicated lanes or compensating threads)'. This starves the pool: blocked workers are cores lost to the frame-critical graph, and on 0–2-worker tiers the frame stalls. It contradicts RES.MGMT.no-stall and CORE.JOBS.degenerate, and it makes the pinned lanes pointless for blocking OS calls.
findings.evidence: TBB uses arenas and dedicated blocking threads; the Go runtime hands off its P on a syscall; the .NET ThreadPool injects compensating threads; Naughty Dog's fiber job system (GDC 2015) parks the fiber, not the thread; Unreal Tasks sends long work to background named threads.
findings.proposed_change: Rename CORE.JOBS.blocking to 'Blocking & long-running work policy: frame-critical workers never block; waits suspend (fiber/coroutine) or move to a bounded blocking/background lane with compensation accounting; long-running tasks on low-QoS lanes with cancellation and budget'. Add the rule to the C-TASK summary. Add a legacy pattern 'blocking calls on frame-critical workers' with CORE.JOBS.blocking as its stance capability.

findings.finding: CORE.OBJ.events is 'global event bus with immediate synchronous listener dispatch by default', which is the exact legacy pattern L19 says this capability replaces. It is a hidden global, it runs callbacks on the producer's thread in the middle of a phase (bypassing C-FRAME access ordering and the phase-violation checks), and it crosses world isolation. Messaging also has two owners: C-ID 'events' and the C-FLOW mailboxes.
findings.evidence: Re-entrancy and ordering hazards of synchronous observers; Bevy moved to buffered Events and explicit Observers; Unity DOTS favours command buffers and event components; mid-phase callbacks cannot be checked by CORE.FRAME.phase-violations or CORE.ECS.safety.
findings.proposed_change: Rename to 'Events & messaging semantics: world-scoped, deferred, batched events consumed at declared C-FRAME consumption points; immediate dispatch only for same-thread same-phase local observers by ADR'. In C-ID, state that event transport is a C-FLOW mailbox: the policy stays with entity-object-model, the mechanism with frame-orchestration.

findings.finding: PHY.ARCH.stepping is 'Variable-timestep stepping on the render frame delta & frame sync', which L30 forbids. It also creates a second authority over simulation cadence, competing with frame-orchestration's fixed-step, time domains and canonical schedule. That breaks C-DET, C-SNAPSHOT rollback and server/client parity.
findings.evidence: 'Fix Your Timestep' (Fiedler); Jolt, PhysX and Havok all recommend fixed substeps; variable dt destabilises constraint solvers and breaks replay and prediction.
findings.proposed_change: Rename to 'Physics stepping within the C-FRAME fixed/declared step (substeps, max catch-up, interpolation hand-off); variable step only by ADR for non-networked non-deterministic games'. Add PHY.ARCH.stepping to L30 stance_capabilities.

findings.finding: PLAT.WEB.runtime says 'SharedArrayBuffer required; cross-origin isolation assumed on every host'. That is false for iframe portals, aggregators and hosts without COOP/COEP. It also contradicts the 0-worker design of CORE.JOBS.degenerate, so the web target fails where it should fall back.
findings.evidence: SharedArrayBuffer is gated on crossOriginIsolated (Chrome 92+, Firefox 79+); embedders must opt in with COEP; Emscripten and Unity WebGL keep single-threaded builds for this reason.
findings.proposed_change: Rename to 'WASM threads when cross-origin isolated (COOP/COEP or credentialless), with runtime detection and fallback to the 0-worker cooperative mode (CORE.JOBS.degenerate); memory limits (memory64 where available)'. Make the M2 exit prove the non-isolated web path.

findings.target: frame-orchestration, C-FRAME, CORE.OBJ.world-instances, NET.SRV.density, PHY.ARCH.multi-world, ED.ARCH.pie
findings.finding: Several isolated worlds per process are required (server density, PIE plus editor and preview worlds, match instances), but C-FRAME describes a single per-frame graph. No capability owns N concurrent world schedules on one worker pool: independent cadences and time domains, cross-world fairness and priority, per-world overload isolation and pause/dilation, and process-global versus world-scoped sync points.
findings.evidence: Unreal ticks UWorlds serially in one loop (the legacy default); dense Linux server hosting runs many sessions per process and needs weighted fair scheduling; the actor runtimes that inspired meshing (Orleans, Akka) solve this with per-actor scheduling.
findings.proposed_change: Add CORE.FRAME.multi-world 'Concurrent per-world frame graphs on one worker pool: independent time domains/cadences, cross-world priority & fair share, per-world overload isolation, process-global vs world-scoped sync points', owned by frame-orchestration with contributors dedicated-server, editor-architect and physics-architect. Mention multiple world schedules in the C-FRAME summary.

findings.finding: The C-SYNC oracle belongs to entity-object-model and the C-TASK oracle to animation-architect. Neither can write suites that detect weak-memory ordering bugs, ABA or reclamation races, or starvation and QoS violations, so the hardest foundation code is graded by incapable oracles. robustness-fuzzing already owns QA.ROBUST.concurrency, contributes to CORE.CONC.correctness and sits in a different workstream.
findings.evidence: Lock-free defects surface only under model checking (Relacy, CDSChecker, GenMC) or ARM litmus stress (herd7); Loom (tokio) is a production precedent for oracle-grade concurrency testing.
findings.proposed_change: Set oracle_author of C-SYNC and C-TASK to robustness-fuzzing. Keep the current skills as consumer reviewers. Require model-checking and ARM64/x86 litmus lanes in the conformance suites.

findings.finding: C-IPC carries tool-worker, editor and profiler traffic, plus the shipping out-of-process crash handler; BLD.SYS.dev-surface-exclusion allows shipping surfaces 'authenticated via C-IPC'. The untrusted-input registry has no IPC or shared-memory entry: no validating owner, no fuzz target, no limits.
findings.evidence: Local IPC brokers and crash handlers are recurring local privilege-escalation vectors (the reason Chromium validates and fuzzes Mojo); shared-memory rings are exposed to TOCTOU double-fetch attacks.
findings.proposed_change: Add untrusted input 'ipc-messages': validating_owner core-runtime-architect, parser_owners crash-diagnostics and editor-architect, trust hostile-local, mode harness, limits frame size/rate/schema version with TOCTOU-safe copy-out. Add untrusted-frame validation to the C-IPC summary.

findings.finding: Budgets are 'measured on the reference high-end PC and scaled proportionally to lower tiers'. Memory, bandwidth and latency do not scale proportionally: UMA pools on console and mobile are fixed physical ceilings with OS reservations, TBDR bandwidth behaves differently, and min-spec caches and core counts change which bottleneck binds. The arbiter would then enforce infeasible budgets.
findings.evidence: Shipping practice sets budgets per tier on each tier's reference device, with min-spec binding (console TRC memory limits; Android low-RAM classes).
findings.proposed_change: Rename to 'Per-tier budgets set and measured on each tier's reference hardware (min-spec binding); memory budgets derived from the tier's physical/OS-reserved ceilings; cross-tier scaling only as an initial estimate'.

findings.finding: memory-allocators consumes only C-PAL and C-BASE, yet it implements thread caches, NUMA-aware allocation, cross-thread frees and defragmentation, which need atomics and locks. The allocator therefore duplicates primitives or escapes CORE.CONC.correctness review. C-SYNC depends only on C-BASE, so adding the edge creates no cycle.
findings.evidence: Modern allocators (mimalloc, rpmalloc, TLSF variants) rely on atomic free lists and cross-thread deferred frees.
findings.proposed_change: Add C-SYNC to the memory-allocators consumes list and to the C-MEM requires list. State in C-SYNC that its lock-free node storage uses the C-BASE raw allocator.

findings.finding: The C-TYPES summary still lists a 'vetted hashinggraphic primitives wrapper' (a garbled leftover of crypto primitives), while CORE.TYPES.crypto is owned by security-runtime through C-SIGN. Two contracts appear to provide crypto.
findings.evidence: Contract summary text compared with the capability owner.
findings.proposed_change: Drop crypto from the C-TYPES summary ('keyed/stable hashing'). Move CORE.TYPES.crypto into a security area, or name C-SIGN in it.

findings.finding: Large and huge page policy is covered only for server hosts. Client-side page-size and commit-granularity policy has no owner, although it affects TLB pressure for multi-GB streaming pools, console 64K/2M pages and Windows large pages.
findings.evidence: Console memory APIs expose 64K/2M pages; Windows large pages require SeLockMemoryPrivilege; Linux THP policy changes allocator behaviour.
findings.proposed_change: Rename CORE.MEM.virtual to 'Virtual memory reservation, mapping & page-size policy (4K/64K/2M, large/huge pages, commit/decommit granularity per platform)'.
